security_spec.violation_condition: In QEMU's riscv_cpu_pending_to_irq() at cpu_helper.c:457, when iprio[irq]=0 and the interrupt's default priority is higher than the external interrupt's default priority (i.e., riscv_cpu_default_priority(irq) < extirq_def_prio), the effective priority is coerced to 1 instead of 0. The spec PR defines IPRIO (effective priority for xithreshold comparison) as equivalent to the value reported in xtopi CSR, which is 0 for this case (see read_mtopi at csr.c:2370-2373). The mismatch means priority comparison in pending_to_irq uses 1 while xtopi reports 0, causing interrupts with programmed priority 0 and high default priority to incorrectly tie with (rather than beat) interrupts with programmed priority 1. Additionally, QEMU does not implement the hart-level xithreshold CSRs (mintthresh/sintthresh) at all, so the entire IPRIO >= xithreshold & NIPPRIO_MASK masking condition is missing from emulation.
security_spec.summary: QEMU's interrupt priority ordering uses prio=1 for iprio=0 high-default-priority interrupts, but the spec-defined IPRIO for xtopi/threshold comparison is 0, creating a priority-comparison inconsistency; hart-level xithreshold CSRs (mintthresh/sintthresh) are unimplemented entirely
